I've done a little speaking here or there, but if I'm lucky, the biggest speeches I will give are all ahead of me. There's this one thing, though, that stands out. My best friend from high school asked me to be the best man at his wedding.

Now, the guy was proper clueless. When I asked if I'd give a speech when I arrived a few days before the wedding, he looked confused and was like, "If you want, I guess?" I put it down to the idea that I was stupid to think the wedding would be traditional, and felt mildly hurt. But then, his then-fiance (now wife, obvs) asked me about it the night before, and I said I had one ready.

I wasn't super sure how it would happen during the reception, but I just waited and ultimately I was given a microphone. I tend to do these things much better off the cuff, so I made sure I had a general idea what I was doing, but I didn't rehearse or write anything down word for word.

I started off with a somewhat rambling introduction about myself, how I had no friends when I arrived at my high school, but the groom had befriended me on the very first day. I explained that I was never short of new people to meet because I would always call him up and give him qualifiers like, 'come alone', 'bring some people', or 'I'm setting up the hookah; tell everyone', and attendance would vary accordingly. I discussed how that broadened my horizons and how I made all of the closest friends of my life (proof that I'm a very lucky man, I was able to gesture at them sitting near me at the table) as a result of his friendship that way.

And I capped it all off by saying that I was thankful especially that I had this chance to tell him how much it meant to me and how much it changed my life, because I know that there are dozens and dozens of people out there we've all lost contact with that aren't ever going to get to tell him how much it meant to them.

I felt like it was a reasonably touching speech, and I was very proud to have had the chance to contribute such a personal mark to this important time in their lives. 10/10, would Best Man again.

Great to hear that your best man speech went so well. Just mentioning a personal story about how the groom befriended a stranger like that on their first day speaks volumes about him. More than any string of adjectives could.

A rehearsed speech can sometimes sound like, well, a rehearsed speech. To me, preparing for a speech means having a couple of key topics or stories that you know you want to share, while rehearsing a speech is more along the lines of memorizing words.
